title: Joint low-flow spell lengths showed no clear excess at three Arctic gauges in 31 certified years from 1980 to 2011
abstract: We tested whether shared low-flow spells were longer than expected from separate river-year sequences at Ob-Salekhard, Lena-Kyusyur and Yenisey-Igarka. We used ArcticGRO v20261104 and 31 common certified complete years in 1980-2011. A low day was below the held-out-year calendar-day 20th percentile. The longest August-October run with at least two gauges low averaged 8.68 days. Independent matching within three time groups gave an exact mean of 8.54 days. The difference was +0.14 day; a two-sided conditional test gave p = 0.8904. All six planned checks gave uncertain results. This extends an earlier test of overlap day counts to continuous duration on the same data. It does not establish independence, a trend, a cause or ocean response. Short coverage, threshold and source error, regulation and the year-matching assumption limit inference. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, exact source hashes and an independent arithmetic audit support reproduction. Raw records and record-level derivatives stay outside the publication.
